subject: FluxPay SDK integration — orchestration checklist and rate-safety plan
messages:

Subject: FluxPay onboarding: SDK setup and migration scope

From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Danielle Moore <dani@fluxpay.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-17T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FluxPay onboarding: SDK setup and migration scope

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clear asks. I've put together a compact orchestration checklist below (also attaching a printable checklist PDF). High-level plan we recommend:

1) Sandbox validation (day 0–3)
   - Install Redwood SDK in a sandbox environment (Node + Go snippets below).
   - Verify auth using a test API key; run 100 requests/s sustained for 10 minutes.

2) Endpoint migration prep (day 4–7)
   - Dual-write pattern: send to both your current endpoint and Redwood for 48 hours; compare responses.
   - Validate request/response shape and latency distributions.

3) Rate safety & resilience (day 8–10)
   - Start with conservative client-side limits: concurrency cap to 60 concurrent requests, per-request timeout 8s.
   - Implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429/5xx. See client snippet.

4) Cutover window (target 2026-11-02)
   - DNS CNAME swap in a low-traffic window + monitor token-level cost and 95th p50 latency.
   - Roll back plan: switch DNS back and disable Redwood routing if error budget >5% in first 30 minutes.

Minimal SDK examples (paste these into your infra runbooks):
Node (npm install @redwood/inference):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' });
try {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-std-1', prompt: 'Hello' });
  console.log(res.text);
} catch (err) {
  // retry logic recommended (see below)
}

Go (go get github.com/redwood/inference):
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, redwood.GenerateRequest{Model: "redwood-std-1", Prompt: "Hello"})
if err != nil {
  // handle retry/backoff
}

Suggested retry/backoff pseudo-code (client-side):
- on 429 or 5xx: retry up to 5 attempts
- base delay: 200ms, exponential growth factor 2, max delay 5s
- full-jitter: delay = random_between(0, min(max_delay, base * 2^attempt))
- implement circuit breaker: open after 10 consecutive errors, retry after 30s

I'll attach the one-page orchestration checklist as a PDF for your PMs. We're happy to run a pre-cutover smoke test with your infra team.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-orchestration-checklist.pdf (PDF, 14KB)]

Thanks all — quick operational runbook we validated with the CS and infra teams:

Pre-cutover checklist (owner in parentheses)
- Confirm API key provisioning and role scoping (FluxPay infra)
- Sandbox perf run: 100 rps x 10m (FluxPay dev / Redwood infra)
- Dual-write verification and diff check (FluxPay infra + Redwood SRE)
- Alerting: set a Slack channel, and create a basic PagerDuty rule for error rate >3% (Logan)
- Cost guardrails: set token caps on the test key and alert at 60% spend threshold (Grace)

If cutover goes green: monitor 5m error rate and average latency for 60 minutes before widening traffic. If error budget is exceeded, execute rollback steps in order (DNS revert -> switch off Redwood routing -> escalate).

I'll upload the short runbook and the rate-limit spreadsheet to the Drive link Logan included and invite Samir from your infra team.

On the call scheduling: Wed 2026-10-27 10:00 PT works for us — please confirm and I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
